You can capture a moment, print it out, and then give the photo as a gift or hold onto it. Image quality won’t be all that good, but imperfections are part of the allure. We tested instant camera models from popular brands and landed on a handful that we think are the best. Some aim to preserve the classic experience above all else, while others support companion apps and the ability to print stored photos. Fujifilm’s latest Instax cameras are the best out there for most people. The company’s Instax Mini Evo is a bit pricey, but it produces great-looking images and offers a lot of creative control. If you’re shopping on a tighter budget, the Instax Mini 13 also takes good photos but has fewer features. The Polaroid Flip is the best retro-focused experience (be warned: prints are pricey!), while Kodak’s Mini Retro 3 might be a better purchase for some because its prints are quite affordable by comparison. The best instant camera Fujifilm Instax Mini Evo Score: 8 Pros Cons Great use of dials and buttons Lots of printing flexibility Good battery life Internal storage is limited No viewfinder Where to Buy: $234 $212.8 at Amazon $234.99 at Best Buy $234 at B&H Photo Film type: Fujifilm Instax Mini film / Film size: 2 x 3 inches / Weight: 285 grams / Charging method: USB-C / Companion app: Yes / Other features: LCD screen, smartphone printing Fujifilm’s Instax Mini Evo is a hybrid instant camera that bears a resemblance to its premium X100 line of cameras that cost hundreds more. Its vintage dials and buttons look so stylish that they caught the attention of passersby as I walked around Los Angeles. It’s easy to balk at its price tag, but this camera offers a level of flexibility that sets it apart (and could save you from wasting a bunch of prints). The camera’s dials also let you apply lens options and effects, from retro filters to monochrome shades, and you can even remotely trigger shots from the app. Its 3-inch LCD screen can be used as a viewfinder, and it also lets you preview and select which images you want to print. The camera’s internal storage tops out at 45 images, which is more limited than we’d prefer, though you can send photos from a smartphone to print. Plus, unlike the Instax Mini 13 (a more budget-friendly pick mentioned below), the Evo uses a USB-C port for charging. Read our full Fujifilm Instax Mini Evo review . It’s easy to use (just twist its lens to turn the camera on or off), it outperforms other budget instant cameras we tested, and we like its bright, playful designs. Its biggest improvement over the Mini 12 is its self-timer, with both two- and 10-second countdown options. Meanwhile, the Instax Mini 41 looks more sleek, but it lacks the Mini 13’s self-timer and costs about $23 more usually. The Mini 13 produced more true-to-life photos than the non-Fujifilm instant cameras I tested. I also appreciated the Mini 13’s generously sized physical viewfinder and that it shows your remaining shots, which is useful given that each print costs about $1. Like many instant cameras, it struggles in low light, though the built-in flash brightens dark scenes. The flash can’t be disabled, and it’s very powerful, which resulted in a handful of overexposed shots during testing. It lacks Bluetooth connectivity along with creative shooting modes found on pricier cameras, so you can’t edit photos, apply filters, or choose from different lens effects before printing. oldContent: We Work Remotely: Remote jobs in design, programming, marketing and more https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs.rss We Work Remotely: Remote jobs in design, programming, marketing and more en-US 60 SimpleTiger LLC: B2B SaaS PPC Manager Anywhere in the World 🇺🇸 United States of America Florida PPC, PPC Management, and PPC Campaigns Sales and Marketing Full-Time <img src="https://we-work-remotely.imgix.net/logos/0001/4550/logo.gif?ixlib=rails-4.0.0&w=50&h=50&dpr=2&fit=fill&auto=compress" /> <p> <strong>Headquarters:</strong> Sarasota, FL <br /><strong>URL:</strong> <a href="https://www.simpletiger.com/">https://www.simpletiger.com/</a> </p> <p>SimpleTiger is seeking a strategic, data-driven <strong>Senior PPC Manager</strong>&nbsp;to lead paid media strategy and execution for our B2B SaaS clients. This role is ideal for a seasoned performance marketer with 5+ years of hands-on experience building, managing, and optimizing multi-channel paid advertising campaigns.</p> <p>The Senior PPC Manager will own campaign performance across Google Ads, LinkedIn, Facebook, and Instagram; translate client growth objectives into effective paid media strategies; and deliver clear, proactive communication and recommendations. You will work closely with our SEO, content, design, sales, and product teams to maximize qualified pipeline, customer acquisition, and return on ad spend for a portfolio of SaaS clients.</p> <h2>Key Responsibilities</h2> <ul> <li>Develop and lead comprehensive paid media strategies tailored to each client’s growth stage, business model, target audience, sales cycle, and revenue goals.</li> <li>Independently build, launch, manage, and optimize campaigns across Google Ads, LinkedIn, Facebook, and Instagram.</li> <li>Own campaign setup from end to end, including keyword research, audience strategy, account and campaign structure, ad group development, bid strategies, conversion tracking, budget allocation, and ad creative direction.</li> <li>Monitor and optimize campaigns against core performance metrics, including CTR, CPC, CPL, CPA, conversion rate, pipeline contribution, ROAS, and ROI.</li> <li>Develop and manage testing roadmaps for ad copy, creative, landing pages, offers, audiences, bidding strategies, and campaign structures.</li> <li>Analyze performance data to identify trends, diagnose issues, uncover growth opportunities, and provide actionable recommendations.</li> <li>Partner with content and design teams to develop high-performing ad creative and messaging that resonates with B2B SaaS buyers.</li> <li>Collaborate with the SEO team to ensure PPC strategies complement broader organic search, content, and demand-generation initiatives.</li> <li>Manage paid media budgets responsibly, making informed recommendations on spend allocation, scaling opportunities, and efficiency improvements.</li> <li>Work directly with clients to communicate performance, explain strategy, set expectations, and provide timely, proactive updates and recommendations.</li> <li>Lead client-facing reporting and performance discussions, turning complex campaign data into clear business insights for both technical and non-technical stakeholders.</li> <li>Partner with sales and product stakeholders to align campaign targeting, messaging, and conversion goals with customer insights and business priorities.</li> <li>Build and maintain strong relationships with platform representatives to access platform support, strategic guidance, beta opportunities, and new features.</li> <li>Stay current on paid media platform updates, privacy and tracking changes, B2B SaaS advertising trends, and emerging best practices.</li> <li>Contribute to the continued improvement of SimpleTiger’s PPC processes, reporting frameworks, account
